record.scope: Static inspection only. The official artifact was downloaded to a task-local temporary directory, mounted read-only and non-browsable, never launched or installed, then ejected and removed after inspection.

facts: kAudioHardwarePropertyTapList enumerates tap AudioObjectIDs on the system.
kAudioTapPropertyDescription returns the CATapDescription used to create a tap.
kAudioProcessPropertyPID and kAudioProcessPropertyIsRunningOutput bind active Core Audio process objects to a PID.
CATapDescription.processes describes included or excluded process object IDs.
isExclusive describes inclusion versus exclusion semantics, but neither it nor processes identifies a tap creator.
isPrivate denotes a tap visible only to its creating client, not a public creator attribution API.
SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes accepts kSecGuestAttributePid for a live guest-code reference.
SecCodeCheckValidity validates the live code against that requirement.

runtimeDecision.identity: A descriptor is eligible only when its requirement compiles and a live PID satisfies both Security requirement validation and the recorded Team Identifier.
runtimeDecision.pidRace: The service reads Core Audio, validates the live PID with Security.framework, then reads Core Audio again and requires the same PID and process-object ID. Any stale, exited, reused, or mismatched observation yields no conflict.
runtimeDecision.membership: Waves reads visible system tap descriptions off the realtime path, but makes no ordinary-app public-membership claim. The public SDK exposes no stable tap-to-router creator association, so readable inclusion, exclusive, private, unreadable, and multiple system taps are all unattributable to Wave Link.
runtimeDecision.fallback: When a verified Wave Link process remains actively outputting audio and the ordinary target has active Core Audio output, Waves conservatively uses monitor-only. The returned detail says that public attribution is unavailable and does not claim that the target is Wave Link-owned. An unverified process claiming Wave Link's bundle identifier is not a positive identity signal and cannot trigger this fallback.
runtimeDecision.mixedOutput: Wave Link's own target remains unconditionally excluded by the existing bundle-target rule. The verified provider's router-mixed-output result adds a verified explanation but is not required for that exclusion.

limitations: Core Audio does not expose a public tap-creator PID or other stable tap-to-router association in the inspected SDK headers. The provider therefore never attributes a system tap or its membership to Wave Link.

No running Wave Link instance, configured Wave Link route, or hardware mutation was used. Physical coexistence, configured-route ownership, private-tap visibility, and device-specific behavior remain release-gate work.
